summary.text: Clayton (Clay) Fuller is the Republican incumbent in Georgia's 14th District, which he has represented since April 2026. A former district attorney and Air Force judge advocate, he served as a White House Fellow in 2018-2019 and continues to serve in the Air National Guard. He won the April 7, 2026 special election runoff to succeed Marjorie Taylor Greene and the May 19 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Raised in the North Georgia mountains; according to his campaign survey, he is an eighth-generation North Georgian who lives in Dade County. He was captain of the basketball team at Emory University.

Earned a bachelor's degree in English from Emory University (2004), a Master of Public Administration from Cornell University (2006), and a J.D. from Southern Methodist University's Dedman School of Law (2009); later earned a master's degree in military arts and sciences from the Air Command and Staff College (2020).

Has served in the U.S. Air Force since 2009 and is a Lt. Col. and Deputy Staff Judge Advocate in the Air National Guard, according to his House biography. He was deployed from May to November 2024 as legal advisor to the Combined Air Operations Center at Shaw Air Force Base and Al Udeid Air Base, Qatar.
Served as District Attorney for the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit, a four-county circuit in northwest Georgia.
Served as a White House Fellow from 2018 to 2019, working in the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Defense, including on counter-terrorism matters.
According to his 2020 Ballotpedia survey, founded a company focused on bringing investment to small towns in north Georgia. Ran for this seat in 2020 and lost in the Republican primary.
Won the special general runoff election for Georgia's 14th District on April 7, 2026, defeating Shawn Harris, and took office April 14, 2026, succeeding Marjorie Taylor Greene.
Won the May 19, 2026 regular Republican primary for the seat.
